question: The Citizenship Act, 1955 does NOT deal with ____________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**election**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955 primarily deals with the **acquisition**, **termination**, and **determination** of Indian citizenship.
 
• It does not deal with **election** processes, which are governed by separate laws and regulations in India.
 
• The Citizenship Act has been amended multiple times to address various issues related to citizenship.
 
• Provisions for acquiring citizenship include birth, descent, registration, and naturalization.
 
• Termination of citizenship can occur through renunciation, termination, or deprivation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted by the Parliament of India and has been amended by various subsequent Acts.
 
• It provides a comprehensive framework for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship.
 
• The Act ensures that individuals who meet specific criteria can acquire Indian citizenship and outlines the procedures for doing so.
 
• It also establishes the grounds on which Indian citizenship can be terminated or deprived.
 
• The Act does not cover electoral processes, which fall under the purview of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and 1951.
